entry.title: How I Found a $90,000 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Google (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Google's DevSite stored an OAuth secret inside a readable Flask session cookie and reused it as the cookie's signing key, allowing forged sessions to reach unsafe pickle deserialization. Timing-based tests confirmed unauthenticated code execution across the shared platform, earning a $90,000 bounty. The fix separates signing keys from OAuth credentials and removes sensitive serialized objects from client-controlled sessions.

entry.title: Can we Make React Faster using the React Compiler? (20 minute read)
entry.content:
React Compiler uses cache slots and tracks values that change together to avoid unnecessary work. In a 2,000-row microbenchmark, inlining alone slowed rendering from 444 ms to 1,038 ms by removing per-row caches, while adding block DOM updates cut it to 164 ms. These prototypes illustrate optimization opportunities, with workload and memory tradeoffs still to evaluate.

entry.title: Building Shared Workspaces for People and Agents (10 minute read)
entry.content:
Perplexity Projects uses a lightweight Git forge backed by S3 storage so people and agents can build on durable files from isolated, temporary sandboxes. Submissions must match the latest accepted commit, with stale writers replaying their changes rather than overwriting concurrent work. In production, fewer than 2% of submissions are rejected as stale, with median submit latency below 1.7 seconds.

entry.title: Human PR Review Is Next (12 minute read)
entry.content:
AI code review will increasingly replace reading every diff, shifting human work toward requirements, acceptance testing, and ownership of releases. Independent review models, predefined guardrails, and automated review-and-fix cycles form the proposed safety net. A trading-bot rounding bug illustrates the tradeoff: fast fixes do not erase losses or compensate for gaps in the specification.

entry.title: Why WebMCP Matters (9 minute read)
entry.content:
WebMCP lets websites expose JavaScript tools to agents, reducing the slow, brittle interaction of navigating through screenshots and DOM inspection while keeping users in a shared browser session. Shopify's checkout experiment reported 2.7 times faster execution, 58% lower cost, and 60 successful attempts out of 60 compared with 56 for browser automation. Permissions, human approval signals, and testing against complete agent systems remain open challenges.

entry.title: 38 Things We've Learned About Building AI Products (8 minute read)
entry.content:

Its MCP server has five times as many daily users as PostHog AI, while the install wizard compresses roughly two hours of setup into eight minutes. The advice favors shared infrastructure, observable tool calls, small targeted evals, and UI for reviewing and undoing agent actions.

entry.title: How to Effectively Debug When You No Longer Understand the Code (63 minute read)
entry.content:
Three production investigations, a latency regression, a memory leak, and a kernel-level hang, show how to steer coding agents through unfamiliar systems using runtime evidence. The framework separates facts from hypotheses, compares failures with a control, and requires every proposed cause to satisfy all known constraints. Adversarial reviews should seek contradictions, and reproductions must match the real failure's signals before they can be trusted.

entry.title: The Dirty Pages Surprise: When a Read-Only Query Writes Terabytes (10 minute read)
entry.content:
A MonetDB count-distinct query saturates an NVMe drive with writes because Linux flushes dirty pages from temporary memory-mapped scratch files. Moving the scratch files to tmpfs cuts runtime from 73 minutes to 97 seconds, while workload-specific writeback tuning reaches about 100 seconds without moving them off disk.

entry.title: Speculative Decoding: The Art of Guessing Well (70 minute read)
entry.content:

This detailed walkthrough derives acceptance and speedup formulas, covers EAGLE-3, multi-token prediction, and diffusion drafters, and explains why training for acceptance is different from simply minimizing KL divergence.

entry.title: A Single POST Freezes Any Next.js Server (3 minute read)
entry.content:

The issue affects vulnerable React 19.0 to 19.2 releases and is fixed in 19.0.6, 19.1.7, and 19.2.6.
